controls.reason: Finite replay fixtures over a declared transition inventory cannot prove repeated execution is safe or prevented across every side effect, callback, race, and retry path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted notification side effect fires twice when a migration step is replayed, while every declared database effect is idempotent. The proposed suite passes.

controls.reason: The rule requires explicit before-and-after verification using six named evidence classes, which bound snapshots, formulas, constraints, samples, and invariant results can prove occurred.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a checksum only after transition, totals without a pre-state binding, and an invariant from another migration; exact evidence-class, time, and transition joins fail each.

controls.reason: A protected recovery artifact with immutable identity, access controls, integrity proof, and timestamp before the exact destructive step is a bounded fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a snapshot created after transformation, a writable copy, and an artifact with no restore identity; ordering, protection, and integrity checks reject each. Recovery success is separate.

controls.reason: A field saying rollback is possible does not prove that claim, while the inventory can omit a real point of no return or necessary state condition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration marks rollback possible despite irreversible external notifications and omits that point from the state map. Every listed point has a yes-or-no field, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: For a contract-defined nonrollback state, a versioned roll-forward plan plus authenticated execution against its fixed oracle proves that it was provided and tested.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a plan without execution, a test for a rollback-capable state, and evidence for another transition revision; applicability and binding checks fail each. Universal future recovery is not asserted.

controls.reason: Temporary-copy and credential inventories cannot independently enumerate every database snapshot, export, cache, workstation copy, provider token, and derived credential.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration CSV remains on an operator laptop but is absent from the inventory. Every registered copy and credential is deleted after completion, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The support policy can enumerate five exact lifecycle path types and their supported source and target states in a versioned transition graph.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting downgrade, adding a path without start state, and conflicting support statuses; enum, graph, and version checks reject each. Whether implementations work is not claimed.

controls.reason: Supported starting states are policy-defined and finite, so exact execution records for fresh install and every state-to-target upgrade decide test coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an untested supported version, a fresh-install run bound to another artifact, and duplicate evidence masking a missing state; set equality and artifact joins fail each.

controls.reason: An interrupted-install fixture set cannot exhaust interruption points, filesystem and process timing, partial writes, reboots, and external side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Recovery works at two approved checkpoints but corrupts state if power fails between a rename and metadata update. Every declared fixture passes.

controls.reason: The prerequisite inventory can omit dependencies, and identifying every irreversible change and sufficient prerequisite requires semantic and operational judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An installer deletes the old schema before checking backup credentials; that prerequisite and step are omitted from the contract. Listed irreversible steps check their fields and pass.

controls.reason: Fixture thresholds do not prove all transition paths detect every storage, permission, version, capacity, and connectivity insufficiency before side effects begin.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider quota is exhausted but absent from capacity prerequisites; local negative fixtures all fail early. The proposal passes while transition starts and later fails.

controls.reason: Compatibility during coexistence spans versions, states, schemas, traffic, data, clients, and failure interleavings that a finite matrix cannot exhaust.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Happy-path requests work between adjacent versions, but an old worker misreads a new retry event. Every approved compatibility fixture passes.

controls.reason: An authoritative compatibility matrix and deployment inventory can make the prohibited mixed-version pairs exact, while routing state proves no such pair serves together.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a forbidden pair in one region, a stale matrix, and an instance omitted from the deployment snapshot; complete target joins or freshness checks reject each.

controls.reason: Old-artifact inventories can omit binaries, images, schemas, services, routes, secrets, and jobs, letting them evade owner and cleanup definitions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forgotten scheduled job and secret remain outside the registry while all listed old assets have owners and cleanup dates. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Uninstall evidence cannot prove absence across every access path, listener, scheduler, credential store, replica, cache, backup, and sensitive-data copy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A regional listener and provider credential survive but are absent from the decommission inventory. All declared resources are removed, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Proving no dangling DNS, routes, queues, webhooks, or trust relationships requires complete cross-provider inventories and absence evidence unavailable from declared fixtures alone.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A webhook subscription at an old provider remains active but is unregistered. Every listed relationship is removed, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Supported-consumer inventories can omit variants, and finite compatibility fixtures cannot prove behavior across every client, agent, extension, and external state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A supported browser extension with cached old schema fails after upgrade but is absent from the matrix. All declared consumers pass.

controls.reason: A mechanism can expose exact values yet remain unclear to users or operators, so record and fixture checks cannot decide the full clarity claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The CLI prints an opaque build hash and hidden support code requiring a lookup table. Tests find both fields, but informed users cannot identify version or support status clearly.

controls.reason: Adoption telemetry cannot prove complete device and deployment coverage, while stranded status and actionable detection depend on policy and connectivity context.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Offline clients never report and are omitted; dashboards show all observed versions supported. The proposal passes while a large stranded version population exists.

controls.reason: Authenticated acceptance criteria with an effective timestamp before the recorded development-complete event fully decide this ordering requirement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried criteria created afterward, a draft without effective status, and a timestamp for another release; status, release, and time joins reject each. Criteria quality is not claimed.

controls.reason: The acceptance-criteria schema has ten explicitly named subjects, so exact nonempty sections bound to the transition decide inclusion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting privacy, merging capacity into cost with no capacity rule, and using a stale runbook link; topic and freshness validation reject each.

controls.reason: An authority registry can identify the exact organization and individual identities currently authorized to accept operational responsibility.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a team without individuals, an expired role grant, and a person from another service; identity, authority, scope, and freshness checks fail each. Wisdom of delegation is separate.

controls.reason: Document presence does not prove substantive architecture, recovery, or known-risk coverage, and the known-risk and dependency inventories can omit material items.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Seven files exist but contain placeholders, and an undocumented provider dependency and risk are absent. Link checks pass while the required documentation is incomplete.

controls.reason: Outstanding-item registers cannot independently prove every incident, defect, exception, workaround, debt item, and supplier commitment was captured and transferred.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A verbal supplier commitment and hidden production workaround are omitted; every registered item has a receiving owner. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: A deployment inventory can omit targets, and monitor presence does not establish meaningful coverage of actual dependencies, failure modes, and user outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A manually deployed regional worker has no monitor but is absent from inventory; listed services have shallow health checks. All joins pass while production coverage is incomplete.

controls.reason: Four explicitly named support routes can each be exercised with authenticated delivery, recipient, timing, and acknowledgment evidence for the exact handover.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a page without acknowledgment, status communication to the wrong audience, and an expired provider contact; route-specific or freshness checks reject each.

controls.reason: Which runbooks are common or severe and whether an exercise meaningfully represents them requires operational judgment; inventories can omit difficult procedures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A trivial restart is labelled severe and exercised, while database corruption is omitted. Every declared common and severe runbook has a receiving-team record, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Finite exercises cannot verify backup restoration, rollback, failover, and credential recovery across all failure states, data shapes, dependencies, and expiry conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The four happy-path drills pass, but restoring an older encrypted backup fails after key rotation. Approved fixtures pass while a procedure remains invalid.

controls.reason: High-risk transition classification requires accountable risk judgment, and a transition can be downgraded or omitted before bounded-support-period checks run.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A financially consequential migration is labelled ordinary and gets no enhanced support. Every transition marked high-risk has start and end times, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: A versioned overlap interval and decision-area matrix can assign one current accountable owner to each area, fully deciding the definition fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a gap between delivery and operations, two conflicting owners, and an expired authority record; interval, uniqueness, and authority checks reject each.

controls.reason: The rule asks for measurement of five named early-life subjects; a defined early-life window and metric records with units, sources, and observations prove occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried no user-outcome metric, data integrity without a formula, and observations outside the window; category, schema, and time checks reject each. Favorable outcomes are not required.

controls.reason: A document can list profile metadata but cannot prove it captures the exact extensions and interpretations actually used by every integration implementation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A consumer applies an undocumented enum interpretation while both sides reference the same versioned profile. Record fields pass despite runtime interpretation drift.

controls.reason: Applicable normative requirements and complete conformance claims require standards expertise; a declared test suite can omit or misinterpret a mandatory clause.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A profile claims conformance after tests exclude a conditionally mandatory requirement. All registered tests pass, but specialist reading shows the claim is invalid.

controls.reason: Standard and guidance inventories can omit issuing bodies, profiles, errata channels, and security notices; a configured subscription does not prove active monitoring.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A security erratum for an extension is published on an unlisted channel. Every registered feed is current, so the proposal passes while guidance is missed.

controls.reason: Version and review records are bounded, but whether conformance tests are representative of normative behavior and real implementations is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A suite covers only common valid messages yet is approved as representative; boundary and error behavior is absent. Metadata passes while representation is inadequate.

controls.reason: The portability policy names twelve closed asset categories and can require an explicit portable or not-required decision and scope for each.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting prompts, leaving keys unspecified, and using an unknown category value; exact category-set and enum validation reject each. Portability implementation is separate.

controls.reason: Format documentation and a successful parser run do not establish that a format is durable or independently parseable across time, tools, and complete exports.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A custom format parses only with an unpublished project library and mutable online schema, yet the fixture parser succeeds. The proposal passes without durable independent interpretation.

controls.reason: `Enough` metadata and correct interpretation require semantic and user judgment; schema field presence cannot prove units, meanings, nulls, and relationships are understood.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The export includes field names but omits that amounts are minor currency units. All required metadata slots are nonempty, yet an independent consumer interprets values incorrectly.

controls.reason: Finite round-trip fixtures cannot prove preservation of every relationship, ordering rule, provenance chain, and integrity constraint over all data shapes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Simple fixtures round-trip, but a cyclic relationship loses provenance and tie ordering on a larger dataset. Every approved case passes.

controls.reason: The statement requires an import test into one alternate implementation or a tested documented reconstruction path; authenticated execution proves that occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a parser from the original implementation, a reconstruction document with no execution, and evidence for another export version; independence, execution, and version checks fail each.

controls.reason: A scoped exit exercise can record the five named quantities with units, method, interval, and participant-role evidence, making measurement occurrence exact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried missing downtime, cost without currency, and expertise estimated with no role or hours; schema checks reject each. Whether the exercise predicts every future exit is not asserted.

controls.reason: Required-key inventories can omit keys, and current availability or one recovery exercise does not prove controlled recovery will remain possible under disaster and revocation states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider-held signing key is omitted; registered keys recover in the test. The proposal passes although a required export signature can no longer be validated.

controls.reason: A transition plan can define transfer procedures for four explicitly named trust-asset categories with owner, target, sequence, and acceptance state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting domains, a certificate plan without target ownership, and identities linked to another transition; topic and scope checks reject each. Successful transfer is separate.

controls.reason: Old-provider access and residual-data inventories cannot prove absence across backups, logs, replicas, caches, support tools, credentials, and provider-controlled systems.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider retains a backup and support token not listed in the exit manifest. Every declared asset is removed, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: A negative fixture on declared interfaces cannot prove the old system cannot accept authoritative writes through queues, jobs, database paths, admin tools, or cached credentials.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An old batch API still updates records but is absent from the endpoint set. Listed APIs reject writes after cutover, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: A residual-dependency record cannot independently discover every remaining provider call, identifier, credential, data copy, contract, and operational reliance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A DNS dependency on the old provider remains but is omitted. Every recorded residual dependency has complete fields, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Requirement inventories can omit integration obligations, and whether tests are representative and evidence actually supports each contract requires contextual review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A partner timeout requirement is absent; listed requirements link to trivial happy-path tests. Every row traces successfully while integration assurance remains incomplete.

controls.reason: The rule is test occurrence for four explicitly named integration failure conditions, which distinct authenticated fixtures and bound outcomes can prove.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried using duplicate delivery as ambiguous outcome, omitting reconciliation, and stale partial-completion evidence; category identity and revision checks reject each.

controls.reason: Critical-participant classification and completeness require risk judgment, while `nonconforming` spans an unbounded set of malformed, delayed, inconsistent, and adversarial behaviors.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A payment provider's inconsistent duplicate response is untested because the provider is labelled noncritical. Every declared participant has two fixtures, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Whether traces permit diagnosis is contextual, and identifying restricted or unnecessary data across all log values requires security and privacy authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A fixture trace follows one request, but production correlation breaks at an async boundary and error logs expose a customer identifier. Declared tests pass while diagnosis and privacy fail.

controls.reason: Immutable release artifacts can bind the exact integration baseline, evidence set, exception records, and component versions to one release digest.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing exception file, a component version without digest, and evidence from another release; completeness, integrity, and release joins reject each. Evidence adequacy is not asserted.
